correctness.rationale: The exact diagonal polynomial kernel is guaranteed by Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2610.17527v1. Its Fubini--Study pullback gives radial and angular variance identities; the two highest nonzero degrees have relative masses \(1-O(t^{-2})\) and \((A_{m-1}/A_m)t^{-2}+O(t^{-4})\). Their positive ratio yields radial speed \(\sqrt{A_{m-1}/A_m}\,t^{-2}+O(t^{-4})\), integrating to \(\sqrt{A_{m-1}/A_m}\,t^{-1}+O(t^{-3})\). Comparing top-degree projective monomial coordinates proves the if-and-only-if phase quotient; Fubini--Study distance is bounded above by intrinsic Bergman distance; compactness and uniform ray tails prove an embedded completion torus. All quantifiers and normalization appear in RESULT.md; finite algebra diagnostics are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The newly studied unbounded horn domains have explicitly computable finite-dimensional Bergman spaces but unknown global metric completion geometry. The finding constructs and classifies a continuum of missing metric boundary points, gives a sharp intrinsic rate in terms of adjacent polynomial degrees, and identifies limiting positive phase-quotient geometry for arbitrary admissible degree. These results locate genuine incompleteness beyond qualitative local positive curvature or routine finite calculations; limitations on full completion and intrinsic boundary metric are precise.
